transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-19
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE); Marco Diaz (Redwood SE); Priya Shah (Redwood Security); Alicia Gomez (CISO, Sable); Tom Reynolds (Head of Vendor Risk, Sable); Mei Chen (Compliance Analyst, Sable)

Quick summary:
Short walkthrough of Sable's vendor security questionnaire (SIG + customer form), focused on encryption/KMS, audit logging, data residency, and SSO/RBAC controls. Identified items needed for evidence handoff and timing for SOC 2 artifacts. Agreed to a follow-up evidence session and pilot for private/VPC setup.

Topics covered: SOC 2 Type II availability of report, control mappings, KMS integrations (bring-your-own-key vs Redwood-managed), audit log retention and export, SSO/SAML & RBAC, data residency in eu-west, dedicated vs hosted deployment, SIG spreadsheet allocation, evidence folder links.

--- Transcript body (timestamps approximate, transcription imperfect) ---
[00:00] Lena Park: Okay good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. I think we have about 50 minutes, we'll run through the SIG and the custom security questionnaire, and then capture action items. Marco, Priya, you good?
[00:08] Marco Diaz: Yep, ready. Hey Alicia, Tom, Mei.
[00:11] Alicia Gomez: Hi all, thanks for making time. We've got a few Sable execs pulled in but this is the main review we need for the vendor risk meet.
[00:20] Tom Reynolds: Quick ask up front: we need to make sure encryption key ownership and residency are explicit. Also curious about audit log integrity and export.
[00:28] Priya Shah: Totally. We'll walk through our key management options — Redwood-managed KMS, cloud KMS integration, and BYOK patterns. Note there might be a small difference in feed when you go Dedicated or Private.
[00:37] Mei Chen: When you say BYOK, do you mean we can bring our HSM from AWS KMS or a third party?
[00:42] Marco Diaz: Yes, you can integrate customer KMS — we support AWS KMS and GCP KMS via connectors. There's also an HSM path for Private on-prem. I should say that on the hosted plan we offer envelope encryption with Redwood-stored master keys by default.
[00:55] Alicia Gomez: And that default - is it multi-tenant keying or per-customer?
[00:59] Priya Shah: Default hosted uses customer isolated keys per account, but the root master is managed by the cloud provider; Redwood maintains a separate DEK per tenant. I might've mangled that — basically each tenant's data keys are unique, but if you need full BYOK with no provider access, we'd recommend Redwood Private or a dedicated instance with your KMS.
[01:15] Tom Reynolds: Okay, can you map that to what goes into the SIG? Like we need the exact control language for the encryption row.
[01:21] Lena Park: Good call — we'll add a control mapping doc to the shared folder. Priya, that's for you to attach the SOC2 sections that correspond to encryption controls.
[01:28] Priya Shah: Yup, I'll upload the SOC 2 Type II and a control mapping PDF.
[01:32] [Speaker 1]: Uh-huh.
[02:10] Marco Diaz: Moving to audit logs — we retain API and admin logs for 13 months by default, with options for extended retention to S3 export. There's an append-only signed log for admin actions and we can provide a snapshot for audits.
[02:24] Mei Chen: Does the append-only signed log use a tamper-evident mechanism? Hash chains, or is that a service log?
[02:29] Priya Shah: We use signed digests and hash chaining for critical admin events; I should caveat that the wording in the questionnaire might say 'log signing' — we'll provide the technical note. Also we'll provide an example export.
[02:40] Alicia Gomez: And can we ship logs to our SIEM in real time? We use Splunk for ingestion.
[02:45] Marco Diaz: Yes, we support real-time export via webhook or streaming to S3 which you can forward to Splunk. There can be a little delay in batching but it's near-real-time.
[03:05] Tom Reynolds: Data residency — we need all customer data for Sable to remain in eu-west if possible. Can Redwood pin region for Hosted?
[03:12] Lena Park: Yes — we have region pinning. For hosted accounts we can store and serve data from eu-west-1 region. For full legal control and auditability you may want Redwood Private in your VPC or Dedicated with reserved capacity in eu-west.
[03:25] Mei Chen: What's the difference between Dedicated and Private around network isolation?
[03:28] Marco Diaz: Dedicated is single-tenant GPU pools managed by Redwood but still on our control plane — network isolation at the VM / container level, predictable throughput. Private is customer-managed control plane: you run the control plane in your VPC or on-prem; you own the network and keys if you choose BYOK.
[03:44] Alicia Gomez: So for our auditors, Private is cleaner because we can show we control the control plane?
[03:48] Priya Shah: Correct. Private gives you the auditable separation. That said, Dedicated with BYOK plus strict contract terms can often meet audit needs.
[04:02] [00:04] Speaker 2: Mm-hmm.
[04:20] Tom Reynolds: On the SIG file, section 5 asks about administrative RBAC and SSO. We need specifics: SAML 2.0 support, SCIM for provisioning, ability to enforce MFA and role-based restrictions.
[04:34] Marco Diaz: We support SAML 2.0, OIDC, and SCIM for provisioning. RBAC is role-based with customizable roles and resource scoping — you can limit who calls the admin API, who can deploy models, etc.
[04:47] Mei Chen: Will you provide a sample ACS and metadata for SAML?
[04:50] Lena Park: We'll share SAML metadata and a guide for SCIM mapping. I'll put the metadata link in the notes after the call.
[04:56] Alicia Gomez: How about session logging for SSO events?
[05:00] Priya Shah: All SSO authentication events are logged and can be forwarded. We keep auth logs with userID, timestamp, IP, SSO provider assertion ID.
[05:08] Tom Reynolds: Good. Next — supply chain and third-party dependencies. Do you have an SBOM or list of critical dependencies?
[05:15] Marco Diaz: We can provide a high-level software bill of materials for the runtime and list major third-party libs. For full SBOMs, we usually redline an NDA; but we can give a standard dependency list.
[05:26] Alicia Gomez: Can you confirm which managed services you use that could touch data?
[05:30] Priya Shah: At a high level: object storage (S3-compatible), KMS (if customer-managed), identity provider connectors, monitoring/observability stacks. We'll provide a table in the evidence folder.
[05:40] [06:00] Speaker 3: [inaudible].
[06:30] Tom Reynolds: A few SIG-specific items: the CAIQ section asked about model provenance and ability to restrict model downloads. We need to know whether model weights ever leave the provider environment.
[06:40] Marco Diaz: Model weights are stored in our internal model registry. For hosted they are stored in cloud storage in the pinned region, and are not exposed as downloadable artifacts. For Private, you can host your own model artifacts entirely inside your network.
[06:54] Alicia Gomez: Are checkpoints accessible via API?
[06:57] Marco Diaz: No public download endpoint; only runtime access.
[07:05] Lena Park: Let's talk evidence handoff timeline. We heard auditors often like a bundle: SOC 2 report, encryption key diagram, sample audit log export, SAML metadata, and the completed SIG rows. What's realistic for Redwood to assemble?
[07:19] Priya Shah: We can assemble the SOC 2 Type II and key diagrams within a week, assuming internal approvals. Log samples take a bit longer because we need to scrub and create a synthetic export — about 7-10 business days.
[07:30] Tom Reynolds: That aligns with our legal timeline. If we get SOC2 next week, and logs the week after, we can feed to the auditors the following Monday.
[07:38] Mei Chen: One more - retention policy: you said 13 months by default. Our policy is 7 years for some data classes; can logs be archived to S3 long-term?
[07:45] Marco Diaz: Yes, we can configure long-term export to your S3 bucket for the retention period you need — that would be part of Dedicated or Private contracts. For hosted, long-term export is available as an add-on.
[07:56] Alicia Gomez: Regarding encryption at rest vs in transit, is TLS always applied? What ciphers?
[08:00] Priya Shah: TLS 1.2+ enforced, we prefer TLS 1.3. Cipher suites follow modern defaults — we'll attach the cipher list; for higher assurance we can enable strict ciphers in Private deployments.
[08:12] [08:30] Speaker 4: okay
[08:50] Tom Reynolds: About incident response: do you have SLAs for notification windows and forensic artifacts?
[08:55] Priya Shah: We have an incident response policy; for customers we commit to notification within 24 hours for confirmed incidents, and provide related logs and a timeline. For enterprise contracts we can negotiate faster RTOs and dedicated support.
[09:08] Alicia Gomez: Will we get access to your audit trail of who accessed customer data?
[09:12] Marco Diaz: Yes — admin access is logged, and we can provide a redacted audit trail for third-party auditors. For customers on Private, you get full access to control-plane logs.
[09:22] Lena Park: Switching quickly to the questionnaire itself — we pulled a version of the SIG and annotated a couple of rows. Tom, Mei, do you want to screen-share the parts you're most concerned about?
[09:33] Tom Reynolds: I can highlight section 3 on data handling, section 6 on encryption, and section 9 on access control. Let me pull up the doc.
[09:40] [09:50] Screen share noises - doc referenced: /shared/sable/sig-snapshot-v2.xlsx
[10:02] Mei Chen: On the encryption question, we need the exact language: 'Customer-managed keys - yes/no; vendor access to key material - yes/no; key rotation policy'. Can you confirm rotation frequency?
[10:14] Priya Shah: Rotation for DEKs is automatic on a rolling schedule, and CMKs if you're using your KMS, rotation follows your KMS policy. We'll give the standard intervals (90 days for some internal keys, configurable for BYOK).
[10:27] Tom Reynolds: We also need a statement about backups — are backups encrypted with same keys and where are they stored?
[10:32] Marco Diaz: Backups are encrypted at rest using the DEK and stored in the same region. If you use BYOK, backups are encrypted with the keys you supply.
[10:40] Alicia Gomez: For evidentiary purposes, we probably need a one-page diagram of key flow.
[10:44] Lena Park: We'll include a key flow diagram in the evidence pack. Priya, can you handle that?
[10:48] Priya Shah: Yep.
[11:55] [11:58] Speaker 5: hmm
[12:10] Tom Reynolds: A question about supply chain: do you run vulnerability scans on images?
[12:15] Marco Diaz: Yes — container images go through a vulnerability scan; we maintain patch timelines and can provide a high-level attestation.
[12:24] Mei Chen: Are you SOC 2 Type II cover things like change management and patching?
[12:28] Priya Shah: Yes, our SOC 2 covers change management, access controls, and monitoring — we'll map the specific control IDs to the SIG questions.
[12:36] Lena Park: About the custom customer form — there are a few free-text items where Sable's legal wants assertive language on jurisdiction. We can supply contract language for data residency and subpoena responses.
[12:48] Alicia Gomez: Important: we require 30 day notice for changes to data handling. Is that feasible?
[12:53] Lena Park: We can include a contract clause for 30 day notice for data handling changes in enterprise agreements. I'll loop legal on that.
[13:02] Tom Reynolds: Can you provide sample SLAs for Dedicated? Latency targets, uptime, and throughput?
[13:08] Marco Diaz: Yes — Dedicated has reserved throughput guarantees and SLA targets for latency tail percentiles; I'll share the SLA doc. For TTF-1 and 99th percentile numbers, we'll include the benchmark sheet.
[13:20] Mei Chen: On the model side, we need to show model vetting. Do you do red-team or content filtering?
[13:27] Marco Diaz: We provide guardrails and content filters; model evaluation tooling is part of Redwood Optimize. For regulated use-cases we recommend private models and stricter evals.
[13:38] Alicia Gomez: Any history of breaches?
[13:40] Priya Shah: We have had no security incidents impacting customer data in the last 36 months; that's in our security whitepaper. We'll include that statement in the evidence pack.
[13:49] Lena Park: Okay we're about two thirds through, let's capture explicit deliverables.
[13:53] Tom Reynolds: We'll need: SOC2 report, control mapping, key flow diagram, sample log export, SAML metadata, completed SIG rows. That's our list.
[13:59] Priya Shah: Noted. Also, for the sample log export, please confirm which data classes you want redacted and which fields must remain.
[14:05] Mei Chen: Keep user identifiers hashed but preserve timestamps and event types. IP addresses can be obfuscated.
[14:12] Marco Diaz: Got it.
[14:30] Speaker 6: [laughter]
[15:00] Lena Park: Last bit — pilots. If Sable wants to run a VPC pilot, we can spin up a Private trial for a two-week window with limited capacity for performance testing. That helps get ahead of residency and key issues.
[15:12] Alicia Gomez: That sounds good. What's the expected lead time?
[15:15] Marco Diaz: About 10 business days to provision a Private trial environment with basic network config. If you want BYOK with your HSM we'll need access details.
[15:25] Tom Reynolds: We'll need an internal approval; could you send a runbook for the pilot steps?
[15:29] Lena Park: Yes, we'll send a pilot runbook and checklist.
[15:33] Priya Shah: Also note: for performance we recommend sending representative traffic patterns, especially prompt sizes and concurrency targets. That helps us tune batching and KV cache behavior.
[15:46] Mei Chen: We'll prepare that.
[16:02] [16:10] Speaker 7: okay ok
[16:30] Tom Reynolds: A slightly nitty point — regulatory retention. If a regulator demands data, how does Redwood handle legal requests?
[16:39] Priya Shah: We respond to lawful requests per our policy and our contract terms; for Private deployments you can enforce your own legal process since the control plane is in your VPC. We'll include our legal contact and subpoena handling process.
[16:55] Alicia Gomez: Are there any sub processors that might be outside eu-west?
[16:59] Marco Diaz: Some telemetry services live in other regions; we'll provide a list and residency mapping. For strict residency we recommend Dedicated/Private and contract clauses.
[17:10] Lena Park: Great. We're approaching the final, let's recap and confirm dates.
[17:15] Lena Park: Action items recap: Priya to upload SOC2 and control mapping by 2026-10-26; Lena to send SAML metadata and pilot runbook by 2026-10-22; Tom to populate the SIG sections 1-3 by 2026-10-23; schedule evidence handoff week of 2026-10-26. Any objections?
[17:31] Tom Reynolds: No objections.
[17:33] Mei Chen: Sounds good.
[17:35] Alicia Gomez: Thanks everyone. Please share all links to the secure folder, not to a public drive.
[17:40] Lena Park: We'll send links with restricted access.
[17:45] Marco Diaz: I'll follow up with the SLA and benchmark sheet.
[17:50] Priya Shah: And I'll prep the key flow diagram and the signed log technical note.
[17:55] [18:00] Speaker 8: bye

End of call.
